source_text: Qui sedent super cathedram Moysi omnia opera sua faciunt ut ab hominibus videantur. Onus legis corporale grave est; jugum Christi suave et onus leve — Evangelium lex spiritalis. Claudunt regnum caelorum nec ipsi intrant nec alios introire sinunt. Gloria Christo. Amen.
thought_title: The Scribes' Burden, Yoke, and Shut Kingdom
orientation: Origen is commenting on Jesus' woes against the scribes and Pharisees, just after explaining that all pretended righteousness is dead.
pass_a_gloss: Those who sit upon Moses' seat do all their works so that they may be seen by men. The bodily burden of the law is heavy; the yoke of Christ is sweet and the burden light — the Gospel is a spiritual law. They shut the kingdom of heaven, and neither do they themselves enter nor do they allow others to enter. Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'Moses' seat' for cathedra Moysi, avoiding 'chair of Moses' or 'teaching chair of Moses.'

choices.term: jugum Christi suave et onus leve
choices.english: the yoke of Christ is sweet and the burden light
choices.why: Keeps the exact contrast between the heavy bodily burden of the law and the sweet yoke and light burden of Christ, preserving the adjectives as predicates.
rejected: Christ's yoke is easy and his burden is light

choices.english: the Gospel is a spiritual law
choices.why: Renders the noun phrase lex spiritalis as 'a spiritual law' to preserve the predicative force of the sentence, matching the letter-spirit contrast in the glossary.
rejected: the Gospel is the spiritual law

choices.term: nec ipsi intrant nec alios introire sinunt
choices.english: neither do they themselves enter nor do they allow others to enter
choices.why: Preserves the double negation and the two finite verbs, keeping the parallel structure of the accusation.
rejected: they neither enter nor let others enter

pass_b_english: Those who sit on Moses' seat do all their works to be seen by others (Matthew 23:2-3, 5). The bodily burden of the law is heavy; the yoke of Christ is sweet and the burden light (Matthew 11:30) — the Gospel is a spiritual law. They shut the kingdom of heaven, neither entering themselves nor allowing others to enter (Matthew 23:13). Glory to Christ. Amen.
